name: Iraq
summary: Red, white and black horizontal bands with the takbir, 'Allahu Akbar', in green Kufic script in the centre. The Pan-Arab tricolour dates to 1963; the current version was adopted in 2008, removing three green stars associated with the Ba'ath Party.
origin: The Kingdom of Iraq used a black-white-green flag with a red trapezoid and two stars. After the 1958 revolution, Abd al-Karim Qasim's republic used a flag with a red-and-gold sun. The Ba'athist government adopted a red-white-black tricolour with three green stars in 1963, modelled on the proposed union with Egypt and Syria.

During the Gulf War in 1991, Saddam Hussein added 'Allahu Akbar', reportedly in his own handwriting. In 2004 the interim government replaced the handwriting with Kufic script, and in 2008 Parliament removed the three stars.

facts: The 2008 flag was adopted as a temporary design; Parliament has debated replacing it several times.
The Kurdistan Region of Iraq has its own flag: red, white and green with a golden sun.
clues: Red, white and black bands with green Arabic script in the centre.

Its tricolour dates from a proposed union of three Arab states in 1963.
